transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net customer service, my name is Danielle. How can I assist you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Danielle. I'm calling about an issue with my mobile account. Thirty days ago I sent in my old Samsung Galaxy S21 under your trade-in promotion for a promised one hundred and fifty pound bill credit, but my latest invoice arrived today with zero credit applied and the full monthly charge debited!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can completely understand how frustrating that is, Gabriel, especially when you returned your handset thirty days ago expecting that trade-in credit to appear. Let me investigate that warehouse intake and sort this out for you right away.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Danielle. I have the trade-in quote email and the Royal Mail tracking slip right here.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's very helpful. Before we access the logistics records, let's complete account verification. Could you verify your full name and billing address?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Gabriel Santos, 82 Victoria Road, Birmingham, B6 5HE.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And what is the security PIN on your account, Gabriel?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Gabriel, verification is complete. So what I understand is you traded in your Samsung Galaxy S21 thirty days ago for an agreed trade-in credit of one hundred and fifty pounds, but your latest invoice did not apply the promotional deduction, and you want that credit applied to your statement today, is that right?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, exactly that. The trade-in quote number was TRD-99410.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What was the condition of the Samsung S21 when you posted it in the pre-paid trade-in pack?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It was in pristine condition. No scratches on the glass, battery health at ninety percent, and fully factory reset.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And what date did you drop the trade-in box off at the Post Office?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: On September twentieth, at the Birmingham Central branch.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Bear with me for a moment while I query the trade-in warehouse intake ledger in our logistics portal.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for waiting, Gabriel. I have located the trade-in record under quote reference TRD-99410 at our recycling depot in Hinckley.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What does the warehouse intake report say?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The phone was inspected on September twenty-fourth and graded as 'Grade A Excellent Condition' with full one hundred and fifty pound valuation confirmed.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So the phone was approved, but the money just wasn't applied to my account?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, it appears the automated billing bridge between the warehouse system and our billing platform encountered a batch sync timeout on the twenty-fifth.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's really sloppy system integration. If I hadn't checked my bank statement, I would have overpaid by a hundred and fifty quid!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You are completely right to be annoyed about that, Gabriel. It is our responsibility to make sure trade-in credits apply automatically without customers having to chase us, and I apologize for the oversight.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I appreciate the apology Danielle. Can you apply the credit today?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I will take direct ownership of this right now. I have manual supervisor authorization to override the failed sync and credit the full one hundred and fifty pounds directly to your ledger.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's wonderful. Will that adjust the invoice that was just generated?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Also, does your new handset have the S-Net Protect device insurance active?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I didn't take out the insurance when I ordered the new phone.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's completely fine. Just keep in mind that our manufacturer warranty covers hardware faults for twenty-four months.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good to know the warranty is two full years.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And you can track all future device trade-ins or upgrades through the Rewards tab on the My S-Net app.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I'll definitely keep an eye on the Rewards tab next time I upgrade.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And your trade-in pack receipt from Royal Mail can be discarded now that the credit is formally credited.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Great, glad I can finally shred that receipt.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes. Your current invoice of one hundred and seventy-four pounds will have the one hundred and fifty pound credit deducted immediately, reducing your outstanding balance to just twenty-four pounds.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And when will my direct debit be adjusted?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: While we are on the line, how are you finding the 5G network coverage around Birmingham?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The 5G speeds in the city center have been incredible, easily over three hundred megabits.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: We recently upgraded the carrier aggregation cells on the New Street exchange, so throughput has improved significantly.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it's noticeably faster when streaming video on the train.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The direct debit collection instruction has been updated with BACS right now to collect only twenty-four pounds on November first.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is fantastic. Can you send me a revised invoice showing the deduction?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously I cannot re-issue the PDF that was already published, but I can dispatch an official credit memo statement directly to your email.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That works perfectly as long as I have it in writing.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to confirm the trade-in reference for the memo audit trail, it was TRD-99410, correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, TRD-99410.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Generating the credit memo now... It has been sent to your email on file, gabriel dot santos at gmail dot com.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me check my phone to make sure it comes through.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, the credit memo email just arrived! It shows one hundred and fifty pounds credit and an adjusted balance of twenty-four pounds.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Can you confirm you see the updated balance of twenty-four pounds on your My S-Net mobile app as well?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Refreshing the app now... Yes, 'Current Amount Due: £24.00 due on 1st November'.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to verify your mobile number on file, it's 07700 900742, correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that's my mobile number.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there anything else with your mobile plan, trade-in, or billing that I can help you with today, Gabriel?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No Danielle, you have sorted out the entire issue quickly and professionally. Thank you so much for your help.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It was an absolute pleasure. Thank you for choosing S-Net, Gabriel, and have a wonderful day.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Danielle, goodbye.
